# Materialized views support collation, except collated aggregate sort keys.
# Expected comparisons and grouping follow the documented und:ci semantics.
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/collation-concepts.md

CREATE TABLE scalars.mv_ci_projection_source (word STRING COLLATE 'und:ci');
INSERT scalars.mv_ci_projection_source VALUES ('Apple'), ('banana'), (NULL);
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW scalars.mv_ci_projection AS SELECT word FROM scalars.mv_ci_projection_source;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM scalars.mv_ci_projection WHERE word = 'apple'
=> "1"

# An explicit COLLATE expression also gives the output column its collation.
CREATE TABLE scalars.mv_ci_expression_source (word STRING);
INSERT scalars.mv_ci_expression_source VALUES ('Apple');
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW scalars.mv_ci_expression AS SELECT COLLATE(word, 'und:ci') AS word FROM scalars.mv_ci_expression_source;
SELECT word = 'apple' FROM scalars.mv_ci_expression
=> "true"

# Do not depend on which spelling represents a collated group.
CREATE TABLE scalars.mv_ci_group_source (word STRING COLLATE 'und:ci');
INSERT scalars.mv_ci_group_source VALUES ('Apple'), ('apple'), ('banana');
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW scalars.mv_ci_group AS SELECT word, COUNT(*) AS n FROM scalars.mv_ci_group_source GROUP BY word;
SELECT n FROM scalars.mv_ci_group WHERE word = 'APPLE'
=> "2"

# Value-returning aggregates retain the input collation, not a comparison key.
CREATE TABLE scalars.mv_ci_min_source (word STRING COLLATE 'und:ci');
INSERT scalars.mv_ci_min_source VALUES ('apple'), ('Zebra');
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW scalars.mv_ci_min AS SELECT MIN(word) AS word FROM scalars.mv_ci_min_source;
SELECT word = 'APPLE' FROM scalars.mv_ci_min
=> "true"

# Collation affects the definition's filter even if no collated column is output.
CREATE TABLE scalars.mv_ci_filter_source (word STRING COLLATE 'und:ci');
INSERT scalars.mv_ci_filter_source VALUES ('Apple'), ('apple'), ('banana');
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW scalars.mv_ci_filter AS SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM scalars.mv_ci_filter_source WHERE word = 'APPLE';
SELECT n FROM scalars.mv_ci_filter
=> "2"
